raw_response:
I am thinking about this year now. My land is 20.4 mu. I have been farming 40 years so I know what works here in Quzhou. I went to primary school, so I can read the bag labels and count the money, but I do not study books on farming.

My main crops are wheat and maize — that is the big rotation. I also keep some millet on a small piece, maybe 2 mu, because my family eats it and millet does not need much water or fertilizer. So wheat about 18 mu, maize about 18 mu (same land, two seasons), millet 2 mu in summer on the drier corner.

**Wheat (winter):** Last year I used about 2 bags of compound fertilizer (40kg each, 15-15-15) per mu before planting, that is 80 kg. Then at returning green in spring I put urea, about 20 kg per mu. So nitrogen is maybe 15 (from compound) + 20×0.46 ≈ 24 kg/mu. I keep it like this — it worked. I buy Jimai or Shimai improved seed from the dealer, everyone uses it. I water 3 times: before winter, returning green, filling. Spray 2 times for aphids and rust. Plough every 2-3 years, otherwise rotary. I expect 500 kg/mu, good year maybe 550.

**Maize (summer):** After wheat harvest I plant hybrid maize, Zhengdan or Xianyu, no-till with the planter. One bag compound at planting (40 kg/mu of 15-15-15), then urea 25 kg/mu at big trumpet stage. Nitrogen about 17 kg/mu. Water 1-2 times if no rain. Spray once for borer. Expect 550 kg/mu.

**Millet:** Small plot, I save some seed myself, traditional kind. Just a little compound fertilizer, 20 kg/mu. No irrigation, no spray. Maybe 200 kg/mu, enough for the family porridge.

I do not want to change much. Fertilizer price is high but skipping it costs more in yield. Better safe.
